result.title: Rubix: Global Correspondence-Free Point Set Alignment through Assignment Geometry
result.comment: 67 pages, 20 figures. Includes full proofs and experimental appendices
result.summary: Procrustes-Wasserstein alignment jointly estimates a matching and rotation without supplied correspondences, but alternating minimization can stop at suboptimal solutions. Rubix solves the equally weighted planar problem globally under squared Euclidean loss. Each matching $σ$ of two centered $n$-point sets defines a complex correlation $z_σ=\sum_i\bar x_i y_{σ(i)}$. Their convex hull is the permutation polygon: supporting vertices give optimal matchings at fixed rotations, and the farthest vertex gives the global alignment. We prove the sharp bound of $n(n-1)$ vertices for $n\ge2$, answering Rote's rotation-assignment open problem. In exact arithmetic, assignment queries recover the polygon in $\mathcal O(n^5)$ operations. Assignment-based bounds extend the approach to three-dimensional rotations and partial matching at a supplied translation through branch-and-bound. On timed MPEG-7 shape pairs, Rubix attains every numerical reference value in 12 ms on average, 50 times faster than a rotation grid at the same accuracy. Its distances improve gravity-aligned matching of real 3D scans, shape retrieval and noisy crystal classification over alternating minimization.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究无对应关系下的点集全局对齐问题，提出 Rubix 方法，用置换多边形的凸包刻画最优匹配并给出顶点数上界，扩展到三维旋转与部分匹配，并在形状检索、三维扫描等任务上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是点集配准与组合优化的几何理论工作，与 VLM/LVR 内部状态、证据筛选或推理决策缺乏实质联系，且未见可迁移到 latent 推理的具体方法线索。
